title: CoopConnect Employer Hub
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: CoopConnect Employer Hub
Thesis: A centralized employer portal where companies post co-op roles, review ranked Northeastern candidates, and manage placements end-to-end.
Why this frame: This is the schema-congruent employer-relationship-management portal any competent designer would build for a university co-op program—safe, defensible, immediately recognizable to HR partners.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Marcus Reyes
  Role: HR Talent Partner, mid-size Boston tech firm (220 employees)
  Context: Hires 8 co-ops per cycle across engineering, product, and data teams. Currently coordinates reqs through Outlook threads, a shared Google Sheet, and forwarded PDF resumes from three different universities.
  Emotional state: Stretched thin and slightly anxious—co-op deadlines collide with full-time recruiting, and he fears missing strong candidates buried in his inbox.
  Pain points:
    - No single place to see which Northeastern students match his open reqs—he scans dozens of resumes manually each cycle.
    - Scheduling interviews means 6-8 email round-trips per candidate across timezones and class schedules.
    - Offer status lives in his head and a spreadsheet; he loses track of who accepted, declined, or is still deciding.
    - Mid-cycle and final evaluations arrive as PDF forms he must chase managers to complete, then re-key into the university's system.
  JTBD: When a hiring cycle opens, I want to post roles once and instantly see qualified, ranked Northeastern candidates so I can fill all 8 seats with strong fits before the placement window closes.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Co-op Faculty Coordinator (Northeastern): Reviews employer postings for compliance, approves new employer accounts, monitors placement equity, and intervenes when a match goes unfilled.
  - Hiring Manager (Marcus's engineering leads): Reviews shortlisted candidates Marcus forwards, conducts interviews, and submits the structured mid-cycle and final evaluations.
  - Northeastern Co-op Student: Subject of the matches—their skills, prior co-ops, and availability feed the ranking; they accept/decline offers through the linked student app.
  - University Employer Relations Manager: Cultivates the firm-university relationship, tracks the employer's multi-year placement history, and surfaces diversity and skill-coverage reporting.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Marcus posts one co-op role using a template-assisted builder and, within seconds, watches a ranked, skill-matched shortlist of available Northeastern students populate his Candidate Match Queue—each with a transparent why-this-rank explanation.

USE CASES (12) - the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Post a co-op role with template autofill
     Trigger: Marcus clicks 'New Role' at the start of the spring hiring cycle for a Backend Engineering Co-op.
     Flow: He selects a role archetype ('Software Engineering') → the builder pre-fills responsibilities, required skills, and compensation band from his firm's prior postings → he edits two bullets and sets the cohort dates → he previews against Northeastern's posting policy and publishes.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 drafts the responsibilities and ideal-candidate language from the archetype plus the firm's historical postings; a policy checker validates required compliance fields before publish.
     Outcome: A compliant, well-written role goes live in under four minutes instead of the 40 it took copy-pasting from last cycle's doc.
  2. Review AI-ranked candidate matches
     Trigger: Within seconds of publishing, the Candidate Match Queue fills with available Northeastern students.
     Flow: Marcus opens the queue → sees candidates ranked by fit score with skill-overlap chips → expands a card to read the match explanation → filters by graduation cohort and prior co-op count → stars three to shortlist.
     AI role: Embeddings rank student skill profiles against the role's required and preferred skills; Gemini 3.1 Pro generates a plain-language 'why ranked here' rationale for each candidate.
     Outcome: Marcus reviews a focused, explainable shortlist instead of scanning 60 raw resumes—he shortlists in one sitting.
  3. Schedule and track interviews
     Trigger: Marcus shortlists a candidate and clicks 'Request Interview.'
     Flow: He picks two interviewers → the optimizer proposes three slots honoring student class schedules and interviewer calendars → the student confirms one in their app → an event auto-creates with a video link → status flips to 'Scheduled' on Marcus's board.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro reconciles interviewer availability, student class blocks, and timezone constraints to propose conflict-free slots ranked by mutual convenience.
     Outcome: Interviews are booked in one round-trip instead of eight emails; nothing slips through the cracks.
  4. Extend and manage offers digitally
     Trigger: After interviews, Marcus decides to extend an offer to a top candidate.
     Flow: He opens the candidate card → clicks 'Extend Offer' → selects the role, start date, and stipend → reviews the auto-generated offer letter → sends it → tracks live status (Sent → Viewed → Accepted/Declined) on the Offer Management Panel.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 assembles a personalized offer letter from a firm template; a status engine tracks acceptance windows and nudges before deadlines.
     Outcome: Marcus always knows offer status at a glance and never lets an offer expire unanswered.
  5. Onboard and assign a co-op coordinator
     Trigger: A candidate accepts, converting from applicant to confirmed placement.
     Flow: The placement appears in 'Confirmed' → Marcus assigns an internal hiring manager and a start-week checklist → the system links the Northeastern faculty coordinator → onboarding tasks (equipment, accounts, day-one agenda) generate automatically.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro generates a role-specific onboarding checklist and a day-one agenda from the role description and firm defaults.
     Outcome: The co-op's first week is structured before they arrive, reducing ramp friction and missed setup tasks.
  6. View placement history with the university
     Trigger: Marcus opens the Placement History Ledger to prep for an employer-relations review meeting.
     Flow: He filters by year and department → sees every past co-op, their evaluation ratings, conversion-to-full-time outcomes, and retention → exports a one-page relationship summary.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro summarizes multi-cycle history into a narrative ('Your strongest placements have come from Khoury data-science cohorts; conversion rate is 38%').
     Outcome: Marcus walks into the review with evidence of the partnership's value and a data-backed case for next cycle's headcount.
  7. Submit mid-cycle evaluation forms
     Trigger: A reminder fires at the cycle midpoint for each active placement.
     Flow: Marcus's hiring manager opens the Evaluation Center → sees a structured rubric (technical, communication, ownership) → rates and adds free-text notes → submits → the form routes to the faculty coordinator automatically.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 drafts a starter evaluation summary from the manager's bullet notes; sentiment is flagged so coordinators spot at-risk placements early.
     Outcome: Evaluations get completed on time with richer narrative, and the university sees consistent, comparable feedback.
  8. Track diversity and skill-coverage metrics
     Trigger: Marcus opens the dashboard analytics tile mid-cycle.
     Flow: He views skill-coverage gaps across all open roles → sees representation metrics on his shortlist vs. applicant pool → identifies an under-covered skill (e.g., DevOps) → adjusts a role's preferred skills to widen the funnel.
     AI role: Embeddings cluster candidate skills to surface coverage gaps; Gemini 3.1 Pro recommends posting adjustments to broaden qualified-but-overlooked candidates.
     Outcome: Marcus closes skill gaps proactively and supports equitable funnels without manual auditing.
  9. Resolve an unfilled role nearing deadline
     Trigger: A role has 5 days left in the placement window and zero shortlisted candidates.
     Flow: An alert surfaces on the dashboard → Marcus opens 'Rescue Suggestions' → AI proposes loosening one preferred skill and shows the expanded candidate pool → he applies the change and shortlists two new fits.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro simulates how relaxing each requirement expands the qualified pool and quantifies the trade-off.
     Outcome: An at-risk req gets filled before the window closes instead of going dark.
  10. Reuse a strong prior co-op for a new req
     Trigger: Marcus wants to re-engage a high-rated past co-op who is now available again.
     Flow: He searches the alumni-co-op list → filters by 'available next cycle' and 'rated 4+' → invites them to apply directly to a matching open role → status shows 'Invited.'
     AI role: Embeddings match returning students to new roles; Wiki RAG surfaces program rules on repeat placements and eligibility.
     Outcome: Marcus fast-tracks a known strong performer instead of starting cold.
  11. Ask the policy assistant a compliance question
     Trigger: Marcus is unsure whether a remote co-op meets Northeastern's in-person hour requirements.
     Flow: He opens the assistant panel → types his question → gets a cited answer drawn from the university's employer handbook → clicks the source to verify.
     AI role: Wiki RAG retrieves the relevant policy passages from Northeastern's employer documentation and Gemini 3.1 Pro composes a cited, plain-language answer.
     Outcome: Marcus gets authoritative compliance answers in seconds without emailing the co-op office and waiting two days.
  12. Bulk-renew last cycle's roles
     Trigger: A new cycle opens and Marcus wants the same 8 roles republished.
     Flow: He opens 'Prior Cycle' → selects the roles to renew → AI flags two postings with stale skill requirements and proposes updates → he approves and bulk-publishes.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro detects drift between last cycle's skills and current market demand, recommending targeted edits before republish.
     Outcome: All reqs go live in one action with freshness intact, saving an afternoon of re-posting.

KEY SCREENS (10) - every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Employer Dashboard Home - purpose: Single-glance command center showing open roles, candidate funnel, pending actions, and cycle deadlines.
     Primary element: A cycle-progress strip across the top with role status cards below, each showing fill progress and the next required action.
     Motion character: Cards settle in with a gentle staggered fade; deadline-critical cards pulse a subtle amber edge.
  2. Role Posting Builder - purpose: Compose a compliant, well-written co-op role with AI assistance and template autofill.
     Primary element: A two-pane editor: structured fields on the left, live formatted preview on the right with inline AI-suggestion chips.
     Motion character: Autofill text types in with a soft shimmer; the policy checker draws a green checkmark with a confident snap on pass.
  3. Candidate Match Queue - purpose: Review ranked, explainable candidate matches for a posted role.
     Primary element: A ranked vertical list of candidate cards with fit score rings, skill-overlap chips, and an expandable 'why ranked' rationale.
     Motion character: Cards stream in top-to-bottom as scores resolve; the fit ring fills with an arc animation as each candidate loads.
  4. Candidate Detail Panel - purpose: Deep-dive on one candidate's skills, prior co-ops, evaluations, and availability.
     Primary element: A slide-over panel with a skill-radar visualization and a timeline of prior co-op experiences.
     Motion character: Panel slides from the right with momentum; the skill radar draws its polygon edge by edge.
  5. Interview Scheduler - purpose: Propose and confirm conflict-free interview slots between interviewers and students.
     Primary element: A calendar grid overlaying interviewer and student availability with AI-recommended slots highlighted.
     Motion character: Recommended slots glow softly; confirming a slot collapses alternatives with a satisfying snap.
  6. Offer Management Panel - purpose: Create, send, and track the live status of offers across all candidates.
     Primary element: A kanban-style board with columns Sent → Viewed → Decided, cards moving as students act.
     Motion character: Cards glide between columns on status change; an accepted offer triggers a brief confetti-free green ripple.
  7. Placement History Ledger - purpose: Show the firm's full multi-cycle placement history and outcomes with the university.
     Primary element: A filterable table with a sidebar AI-generated relationship narrative and conversion stats.
     Motion character: Rows fade in chronologically; the narrative panel writes its summary line by line.
  8. Evaluation & Feedback Center - purpose: Complete structured mid-cycle and final evaluations and route them to the university.
     Primary element: A rubric form with rating sliders plus an AI-drafted summary the manager can edit before submitting.
     Motion character: Sliders snap to detents; the AI draft fades in beneath the notes field as the manager types.
  9. Analytics & Coverage Tile View - purpose: Surface skill-coverage gaps and representation metrics across the funnel.
     Primary element: A grid of metric tiles with a skill-coverage heatmap and gap callouts.
     Motion character: Tiles count up to their values; the heatmap cells saturate in a wave from corner to corner.
  10. Policy Assistant Drawer - purpose: Answer compliance and program-rule questions with cited sources.
     Primary element: A chat drawer with cited answer cards linking to handbook passages.
     Motion character: Answer text streams token-by-token; citation chips pop in once the answer settles.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) - every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Skill-to-role candidate ranking (Headline aha)
     User action: Marcus publishes a role and opens the Candidate Match Queue.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Role required/preferred skills, student skill profiles (embedded), prior co-op records, availability, graduation cohort.
     Output: A ranked candidate list with 0-100 fit scores, skill-overlap chips, and a one-paragraph plain-language rationale per candidate.
     User benefit: Marcus sees a focused, explainable shortlist in seconds instead of manually scanning dozens of resumes.
  2. Role-description autocomplete
     User action: Marcus selects a role archetype in the Posting Builder.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Role archetype, firm's historical postings, current team context.
     Output: Drafted responsibilities, ideal-candidate language, and compensation-band suggestion.
     User benefit: A polished, compliant posting drafts itself, cutting posting time from 40 minutes to under four.
  3. Interview scheduling optimizer
     User action: Marcus requests an interview with a shortlisted candidate.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Interviewer calendars, student class schedule blocks, timezones, role urgency.
     Output: Three ranked conflict-free time slots with reasoning for the top recommendation.
     User benefit: Interviews book in a single round-trip rather than eight back-and-forth emails.
  4. Evaluation sentiment summarizer
     User action: A hiring manager enters bullet notes in the Evaluation Center.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Manager rubric ratings and free-text notes.
     Output: A polished narrative summary plus a sentiment flag (positive / neutral / at-risk) for the coordinator.
     User benefit: Evaluations finish faster with richer narrative, and at-risk placements surface early.
  5. Placement-fit & rescue predictor
     User action: Marcus views an at-risk unfilled role nearing deadline.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Role requirements, current qualified pool size, historical fill patterns.
     Output: Quantified simulations of how relaxing each requirement widens the qualified pool, with a recommended action.
     User benefit: At-risk reqs get filled before the window closes via data-backed posting adjustments.
  6. Skill-coverage gap clustering
     User action: Marcus opens the Analytics tile view mid-cycle.
     Model: Embeddings
     Input: All open-role skill requirements and the applicant/shortlist skill vectors.
     Output: Clustered coverage map highlighting under-covered skills and overlooked qualified candidates.
     User benefit: Marcus closes skill and equity gaps proactively without manual auditing.
  7. Policy & compliance assistant
     User action: Marcus asks a program-rule question in the assistant drawer.
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: Northeastern employer handbook, co-op policy documents, eligibility rules.
     Output: A cited, plain-language answer with links to the source passages.
     User benefit: Authoritative compliance answers in seconds instead of multi-day email waits with the co-op office.
  8. Relationship-history narrative generator
     User action: Marcus opens the Placement History Ledger before a review meeting.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Multi-cycle placement records, evaluation ratings, conversion and retention data.
     Output: A concise narrative summary of the partnership's strengths, trends, and recommended next-cycle headcount.
     User benefit: Marcus walks into reviews with a data-backed story instead of raw spreadsheets.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: data-forward institutional restraint—Northeastern crimson accents on a calm neutral canvas, editorial typography, generous whitespace, confident-but-not-flashy enterprise polish
  Hero treatment: The dashboard leads with a horizontal cycle-progress strip rendered as a clean segmented bar, beneath which role status cards sit in a tidy grid. The Candidate Match Queue is the emotional centerpiece: ranked cards with animated fit-score rings and crisp skill-overlap chips, conveying intelligence and trust at a glance. Crimson is reserved for primary actions and deadline urgency; everything else stays neutral so the data reads as the protagonist.
  Motion character: Purposeful and reassuring—staggered card entrances, fit-rings that arc into place, text that streams to signal AI reasoning, and snappy confirmations on commits. Nothing bounces gratuitously; motion always communicates state change or progress.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these - the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. A warm, candid editorial photo of a diverse group of college-age co-op students collaborating around a laptop in a modern Boston office, natural light, shallow depth of field
    2. An abstract crimson-and-slate data-mesh illustration suggesting skill-to-role matching, clean vector style on a light background
    3. A confident professional headshot-style portrait of an HR talent partner reviewing a tablet, neutral office backdrop, trustworthy enterprise mood
    4. A minimalist isometric illustration of a hiring funnel turning resumes into ranked, glowing candidate cards
    5. A subtle Northeastern campus-inspired skyline line illustration in crimson for empty-state and onboarding screens
    6. An icon set illustration for co-op lifecycle stages (post, match, interview, offer, onboard, evaluate) in a consistent thin-line crimson style

SUCCESS CRITERIA (Stage 5 audits the prototype against each of these):
  - An employer publishes a compliant co-op role in under 5 minutes from a cold start.
  - Median time from posting to a usable ranked shortlist is under 3 minutes.
  - Interview scheduling completes in a single round-trip rather than multiple email exchanges.
  - Offer status is accurately reflected in real time with zero offers expiring unanswered.
  - Mid-cycle and final evaluations are submitted on time for at least 90% of placements.
  - Cycle fill rate exceeds 95% before the placement deadline.
  - Every AI ranking includes a human-readable explanation, and every compliance answer is source-cited.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
  Brand: Northeastern University co-op program—crimson (#C8102E) primary accent, respect university logo usage and employer-portal tone guidelines
  Platform: web
  Accessibility: WCAG AA
  Other:
    - Compliance with Northeastern co-op program posting policies and eligibility rules
    - FERPA-conscious handling of student data—employers see only program-authorized fields
    - All AI rankings must be explainable and contestable; no opaque scoring
    - Equity guardrails: representation metrics must never enable discriminatory filtering

brief.one_line_thesis: A centralized employer portal where companies post co-op roles, review ranked Northeastern candidates, and manage placements end-to-end.

primary_persona.name: Marcus Reyes
primary_persona.context: Hires 8 co-ops per cycle across engineering, product, and data teams. Currently coordinates reqs through Outlook threads, a shared Google Sheet, and forwarded PDF resumes from three different universities.
primary_persona.emotional_state: Stretched thin and slightly anxious—co-op deadlines collide with full-time recruiting, and he fears missing strong candidates buried in his inbox.

secondary_actors.involvement: Reviews employer postings for compliance, approves new employer accounts, monitors placement equity, and intervenes when a match goes unfilled.
Reviews shortlisted candidates Marcus forwards, conducts interviews, and submits the structured mid-cycle and final evaluations.
Subject of the matches—their skills, prior co-ops, and availability feed the ranking; they accept/decline offers through the linked student app.
Cultivates the firm-university relationship, tracks the employer's multi-year placement history, and surfaces diversity and skill-coverage reporting.

brief.demonstrated_moment: Marcus posts one co-op role using a template-assisted builder and, within seconds, watches a ranked, skill-matched shortlist of available Northeastern students populate his Candidate Match Queue—each with a transparent why-this-rank explanation.
jobs_to_be_done: When a hiring cycle opens, I want to post roles once and instantly see qualified, ranked Northeastern candidates so I can fill all 8 seats with strong fits before the placement window closes.
Post a co-op role with template autofill
Onboard and assign a co-op coordinator

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an expert technical recruiter AI. Given a role's required/preferred skills and a list of student profiles, rank them by fit score (0-100) and generate a 1-paragraph plain-language rationale explaining why they are ranked here based on skill overlap and prior experience.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Role: {{role_details}}. Candidates: {{student_profiles}}. Return ranked list with scores and rationales.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an HR assistant. Draft a compliant, engaging co-op role description based on the selected archetype, the firm's historical postings, and current team context.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Archetype: {{archetype}}. History: {{historical_postings}}. Generate responsibilities, ideal candidate profile, and suggest a stipend band.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a scheduling optimizer. Reconcile interviewer calendars, student class blocks, and timezones to propose 3 conflict-free interview slots, ranking them by mutual convenience.
You are a management coach. Convert raw bullet notes from a manager into a polished, professional evaluation summary. Flag the sentiment as positive, neutral, or at-risk.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Ratings: {{rubric_scores}}. Notes: {{bullet_notes}}. Draft summary and flag sentiment.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a talent pool analyst. Analyze an unfilled role nearing its deadline. Simulate how relaxing specific preferred skills expands the qualified candidate pool and recommend the best trade-off.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Role: {{role_requirements}}. Current Pool: {{pool_size}}. Suggest 1 requirement to relax and predict new pool size.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a workforce analytics engine. Cluster candidate skills against open role requirements to identify under-covered skills and surface qualified but overlooked candidates.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Roles: {{open_roles_skills}}. Candidates: {{applicant_skills}}. Identify top 3 coverage gaps.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a compliance expert for the Northeastern Co-op program. Answer employer questions accurately using ONLY the provided handbook passages. Cite your sources.
You are an employer relations analyst. Summarize multi-cycle placement history into a concise, data-backed narrative highlighting strengths, conversion rates, and trends.
